# Ticket-to-test-plan methodology

Use when the user supplies a concrete Jira-style ticket ID, explicitly requests full QA analysis or a test plan, and confirms the target test branch. Work in **British English**. Do not pause for permission between analysis steps. Ask only for missing required inputs, a failed fetch after one retry, unresolvable ambiguity, or an action gate. Reuse outputs for this ticket already present in the session; rerun only missing or stale steps. If code/branch is inaccessible, record this and continue ticket-description-only analysis. Retain the Generic POC's traceability and risk methodology, but **project-specific commands, stacks, paths and provider conventions come from the approved project layer**, not POC example scripts.

Consult `traceability.md`, `readiness.md`, `dedup-rule.md`, `automation-criteria.md`,
`regression-areas.md`, `artefacts.md` and `questions.md` for the reusable decision
rules below; they are independent methods, not mandatory tool calls between steps.

1. **Requirements analysis and implementation verification.** Extract core behaviours, business rules, validation logic; performance, security, logging and environment-specific expectations; edge cases, feature flags, environmental dependencies, integrations, risk areas, ambiguities and missing information. Assign stable `FR1`, `FR2`, … and `NFR1`, `NFR2`, … IDs; never silently renumber them in later steps. On the *confirmed* target branch, check presence and fidelity of implementation, missing behaviour, scope deviations, flags and environment logic. Report discrepancies separately from unverified claims.
2. **Unit test assessment.** Developers own writing and running unit tests; QA inspects their presence and how convincingly their assertions address the acceptance criteria. Do not imply they were executed by QA. Check positive and negative paths, edge cases, failure modes, appropriate boundary mocks, over-mocking and happy-path-only coverage. Map gaps to the stable requirement IDs. Give specific recommendations and a verdict: **Pass**, **Needs Improvement**, or **Insufficient**. If requirements analysis is absent in an independent invocation, derive requirements from the ticket.
3. **Lean manual BDD scenarios.** Manual scenarios catch real business outcomes, cross-service behaviour and real environment edge cases that unit/integration tests cannot. Before drafting, filter out isolated logic cases that verified passing unit tests already exercise; merge their ACs into larger business flows unless a live integration, flag, permission, significant risk or coverage gap merits direct manual validation. Keep HIGH/CRITICAL risks, runtime feature-flag ON/OFF states, permission concerns and cross-service data flows even in a short plan. Three ACs with strong automated coverage may warrant just **2–4** manual scenarios rather than an AC-by-AC copy. Use reproducible, deterministic `GIVEN`/`WHEN`/`THEN`/`AND`, numbered scenarios with category tags and `Covers: FRx, NFRy`. Include a **Scenarios Not Written** list with IDs and one-line deduplication reasons. Use ticket-linked test-data IDs but natural display names.
4. **Integration and automation evaluation.** Explicitly consider cross-service impact, API contracts/gateway, backend logic, database effects, feature flags, caching, auth, logging, environment configuration and CI impact. When justified, propose end-to-end scope, file layout, real versus mocked boundaries, test data/environment and CI cost or stability; adapt to the *observed* project stack rather than assuming Python/Playwright. Otherwise state why manual testing is sufficient. Propose automation; do not create tests without explicit instruction.
5. **Regression risk matrix.** Complete every row for API Behaviour, Existing Endpoints, Feature Flags, Caching, Authentication / Authorisation, API Gateway, Backend Logic, Database Layer, Data Integrity, Logging / Monitoring, Environment Configuration, CI/CD Pipeline, and Backward Compatibility. Columns are **Area | Risk Level | Why? | Regression Needed? | Automation Update Needed?**. Use **LOW** (minimal impact), **MEDIUM** (targeted testing), **HIGH** (regression required), **CRITICAL** (core functionality at risk). Do not mark all areas LOW without evidence. Escalate for runtime flags, environment-dependent logic, caching/async behaviour, persistence/schema changes, endpoint gating and auth changes. For each HIGH/CRITICAL area, propose targeted regression, automation reinforcement, production impact and, if applicable, rollout validation.
6. **Test plan output.** Assemble summary, QA Summary Table, risk assessment, requirements breakdown retaining IDs, tagged BDD scenarios, justified automation recommendation, regression impact, environment impact, open questions and the **full regression matrix**. Draft in chat; seek design approval **before finalising** the plan. Report missing steps explicitly rather than filling gaps with invented facts. On a non-default branch after orchestrated workflow-plan approval (no extra L1 action gate), save deliverables in the project's configured output location (normally `qa-work/<work-id>/outputs/`) and update `qa-work/<work-id>/index.md`; summarise local changes. Use `<TICKET>_test_plan.md`, optionally `<TICKET>_scenarios.md` (manual scenarios only) and schema-verified `<TICKET>_test_data.sql` only where needed and authorised. Offer later upload of reviewed manual scenarios when ready to test, not immediate publication.

The required QA Summary uses the project's eight-column rollup (which supersedes
the narrower five-field example in the Generic POC):

| Ticket | Readiness | Max risk | Coverage verdict | Scenarios written/not written | Automated/manual/not needed | Run result | Published |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| `<TICKET>` | Green / Amber / Red / unknown | Highest supported matrix risk | Pass / Needs Improvement / Insufficient / Not assessed | Written and deliberately omitted counts with reasons | Evidence-backed disposition | PASS / FAIL / BLOCKED / Not yet executed | Yes with link / No |

Never invent test results, publication state or readiness; mark unavailable evidence
as unknown/not assessed. Preserve requirement IDs and the full 13-area matrix in the
plan regardless of the summary table.

After the plan, if automation is justified, propose (do not create) a branch in project convention, for example `task/PROJ-1234-add_feature_flag_tests`; description length **10–45** characters, starts alphanumeric and contains only letters/digits/`-`/`_`. Explain naming and intended test layout. Offer to run relevant existing automation suites *only after* the user confirms the target environment and execution; tests may require SSO or cloud credentials and may affect shared data. Report actual pass/fail counts, failures and report path when run.

A Jira comment is normally the **last action**, after manual results are known; it can also be requested standalone. Draft the exact plain-text comment in chat with actual manual PASS/FAIL/BLOCKED results, Confluence evidence link, automation PR link if any, and unit/integration coverage only when assessed (with supported test counts, not guesses). Request approval plainly: **“May I publish the comment shown above, unchanged, to `<TICKET>`?”** Wait for affirmative approval for that exact text; after edits ask again. Confirm posting only after the provider succeeds.
